components.css: .ds-dock{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:8px;width:max-content;max-width:100%;padding:9px 10px 7px;border:1px solid #ffffff23;border-radius:20px;background:linear-gradient(#343c45c4,#232b34d9);box-shadow:inset 0 1px #ffffff09,0 12px 35px #0005,0 3px 9px #0003;backdrop-filter:blur(22px)}.ds-dock-app{position:relative;display:grid;place-items:start center;flex:0 0 54px;width:54px;height:59px;padding:0 0 8px;border:0;border-radius:11px;background:none;color:#d2dbe3;cursor:pointer;transition:transform 140ms var(--mh-ease,cubic-bezier(.23,1,.32,1))}.ds-tile{position:relative;display:grid;place-items:center;width:50px;height:50px;border:1px solid #ffffff23;border-radius:13px;background:linear-gradient(145deg,#46505a,#2c343d 46%,#1b222a);box-shadow:inset 0 1px 0 #ffffff12,0 5px 9px #00000030;overflow:hidden}.ds-tile>svg{width:32px;height:32px;filter:drop-shadow(0 2px 2px #0005)}.ds-launch>svg{transform:rotate(-7deg)}.ds-projects{background:linear-gradient(145deg,#53606b,#343e48 52%,#242d36)}.ds-tile>i{position:absolute;right:4px;top:4px;width:7px;height:8px;clip-path:polygon(0 35%,100% 0,100% 65%,0 100%);background:var(--mh-accent,#d7ff00);opacity:.8}.ds-running::after{content:'';position:absolute;width:3px;height:3px;bottom:0;left:calc(50% - 1.5px);background:#9ca9b6;border-radius:50%}.ds-active::after{background:var(--mh-accent,#d7ff00)}.ds-dock-label{position:absolute;bottom:calc(100% + 15px);left:50%;transform:translateX(-50%);opacity:0;pointer-events:none;white-space:nowrap;border:1px solid #ffffff1f;border-radius:6px;background:#282f37f2;padding:6px 10px;box-shadow:0 4px 15px #0005;color:#e5ebf2;font:500 11px/1.4 'DM Sans',sans-serif;transition:opacity 100ms}.ds-dock-app:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--mh-accent,#d7ff00);outline-offset:3px}.ds-dock-app:focus-visible>.ds-dock-label{opacity:1}@media(hover:hover) and (pointer:fine){.ds-dock-app:hover{transform:translateY(-4px) scale(1.06)}.ds-dock-app:hover>.ds-dock-label{opacity:1}}@media(prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){.ds-dock-app,.ds-dock-label{transition:none}.ds-dock-app:hover{transform:none}}

narrative.overview:
A modern working desktop in graphite, cold white, silver and citron. Independent tools sit on a calm branded desk; opening a window gives the task a solid, legible interior. The original angular M appears as quiet relief, with its citron notch intact.

The material is restrained and tactile: matte dimensional app tiles, translucent chrome, thin dividers and soft ambient shadows. The wallpaper's sculpted geometry stays still. Three small points move independently when motion is enabled. English labels describe actual tools and honest states.

This records the implemented OS cascade in `src/os-theme.css`, supported by `motion.css`, `wallpaper.css`, `product.css` and `workspace-design.css`. It captures the approved world in `.impeccable/os-direction.md`; the code, rather than the concept image, determines values. The older `docs/DESIGN.md` is a legacy record.
keyCharacteristics: Graphite task surfaces and silver tool identities.
A single citron accent for action, focus and the brand notch.
Independent windows, a thin top bar and a floating Dock.
A quiet relief M and three restrained points.
Compact text with clear labels and visible keyboard focus.

rules.name: The Citron Has a Job Rule
rules.body: Use citron to identify an action, focus, selection or the established brand detail. Preserve the dark silver field around it.

rules.name: The Glass at the Edge Rule
rules.body: Use translucency for desktop chrome and floating navigation. Keep task interiors opaque enough to read over the wallpaper and other windows.

rules.name: The One App, One Identity Rule
rules.body: Keep the same app glyph and matte tile across shortcuts, Apps and the Dock. Opening, minimizing and restoring must remain connected to that identity.

dos: Do retain the original angular M, citron notch, MemeHelm name and “Launch it. Steer it.” tagline.
Do reuse graphite task surfaces, silver app tiles and the existing two-font hierarchy.
Do keep all tools reachable through Apps, search and the Dock on narrow screens.
Do preserve solid task interiors, visible focus and reduced-motion behavior.
Do show real project state and identify illustrative examples.
donts: Don't animate wallpaper lines, ribbons or sculpted planes; only the three independent points move.
Don't replace this OS world with pastel chrome, retro pixel typography or a dashboard grid.
Don't add a circular plate behind the M, dense dot patterns or invented activity metrics.
Don't introduce decorative eyebrows, hard offset shadows or Unicode substitutes for authored SVG icons as reusable OS patterns.
